"''The ''Silver Angel''? Hmm. You should rethink that.|Trace and Rafa Martez|audio=TheSilverAngel-DND.flac|}} The '''''Silver Angel''''' was a repurposed [[Nebula-class freighter|''Nebula''-class freighter]] assembled and modified by the [[Technician|mechanic]] and aspiring [[pilot]] [[Trace Martez]], who lived on [[Level 1313]] of the [[planet]] [[Coruscant]] during the [[Clone Wars]]. Pulling mostly from spare parts gathered in Coruscant's [[Coruscant Underworld|underworld]], Martez sought to build a [[starship]] much faster than the average ''Nebula'' [[freighter]], adding her own special modifications. The ''Silver Angel'' was a personal labor for Trace, who hoped to craft a vessel capable of taking her away from the planet where her [[Martez family|parents]] were [[Death|killed]]. Work on the vessel was completed in [[19 BBY]], and, after its owner befriended the former [[Jedi]] [[Ahsoka Tano]], the ship saw its first flight when Trace accepted a job from her sister [[Rafa Martez|Rafa]] to ferry [[sansanna spice]] aboard the ''Angel'' from [[Kessel]] to [[Oba Diah]]. When Trace discovered that they were working for the dangerous criminal organization known as the [[Pyke Syndicate]], however, she grew fearful of what the [[crime lord]]s could do to her and her ship and dumped the [[spice]] into [[hyperspace]]. The crew attempted to deceive the Syndicate's leader, [[Marg Krim]], and avoid his wrath, but the [[Pyke]]s saw through their ruse and captured them, impounding the ''Angel'' at [[Pyke Palace|Krim's palace]]. Although the sisters were briefly allowed to leave the planet aboard the freighter after Tano convinced Krim that the spice shipment was off-world, the siblings soon returned in the hopes of rescuing their new friend. After escaping the Pykes' [[Prison|dungeons]], Tano helped the Martez sisters [[Escape from Oba Diah|fight]] their way to the ''Angel'' and flee from the Syndicate's palace before returning to Coruscant, at which point she departed their company with the [[Mandalorian]] [[Bo-Katan Kryze]]. After the [[Proclamation of the New Order|rise]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], the ''Angel'' became a mobile homebase for the Martez sisters as they became [[smuggler]]s, taking work from those who sought to fight back against the newly-formed [[dictatorship]]. One such individual, the former [[Clone Captain]] [[Rex]], sent the sisters to [[Corellia]] to [[Mission to a droid decommissioning facility|obtain]] strategic information from a [[Unidentified T-series tactical droid (Corellia)|decommissioned]] [[T-series military strategic analysis and tactics droid|tactical droid]] to help with his [[Clone Underground|resistance effort]]. During the mission, Trace and Rafa encountered the [[Clone Force 99|Bad Batch]], a group of renegade [[clone commando]]s who had deserted the [[Imperial Military]]. After retrieving the intel, the sisters departed aboard the ''Angel'' and informed Rex about the rogue [[Cloning|clones]]. ==Description== {{Quote|Well, if you're a Jedi, I assume you're a good shot?''"
"''Yes.''"
"''Then shoot something!|Trace Martez gives the ''Silver Angel''{{'s}} guns over to Ahsoka Tano|audio=ShootSomething-TA.flac|}} [[File:SilverAngelLaserTurret-TA.png|thumb|right|300px|The ''Silver Angel''{{'s}} laser turret]] Although recognizably a [[Nebula-class freighter|''Nebula''-class freighter]], the ''Silver Angel'' contained a number of modifications made by its owner, [[Trace Martez]], who streamlined the [[Starship|vessel]] in order to make it faster than the average [[freighter]] and swifter than baseline ''Nebula''-class freighters.''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' The ship's speed was of particular pride to Martez, who often bragged of her vessel's capabilities to anyone who would listen, even before she had actually [[Pilot|flown]] the ship. The ship shared its name with the [[Diathim|Angels]], a [[species]] of beings who inhabited the [[moons of Iego]].{{Film|I}} Assembled from spare parts, the ship measured at 55 [[meter]]s (180 [[Foot|feet]], 4 inches) in length and had a variety of systems, including a class 3 [[hyperdrive]], a communications interface, and [[Atmosphere|air]] brakes, as well as front- and rear-facing [[deflector shield]]s and six [[engine]]s. The ''Angel'' could support a crew of at least three members and had enough capacity to carry at least three containers of unrefined [[spice]]. For offensive capabilities, the ''Angel'' had one ventral retractable [[laser turret]] that could fire in any direction.{{EncyclopediaCite|Miscellaneous Ships and Vehicles (1)}} The ''Angel''{{'s}} spacious [[cockpit]], which was on a different level from most of the ship, had a similar design layout to the [[VCX-100 light freighter]],{{SW|url=deal-no-deal-trivia-gallery|text=Tech's Notes: "Deal No Deal" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 1}} featuring enough space for a pilot, co-pilot, and third passenger. ==History== ===Assembly=== {{Quote|It's not safe down here or anywhere on Coruscant. That's why I've got my ship, so I can make my living in the stars.|audio=LivingInTheStars-GWT.flac|Trace Martez|}} Living in the seedy [[Coruscant Underworld|underworld]] of{{Databank|trace|Trace}} the [[Core Worlds]] [[planet]] [[Coruscant]] with her sister [[Rafa Martez|Rafa]] during the [[The galaxy|pan-galactic]] conflict known as the [[Clone Wars]], the young [[Technician|mechanic]] Trace Martez dreamed of becoming a pilot and flying away in her own starship. Although the sisters had little [[Currency|money]], Trace was determined to realize her dream. By working odd jobs on [[Level 1313]] of the underworld and accepting help from her older sister, Trace was able to earn enough [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] to acquire the materials to build a ship. She assembled her ship piece by piece, constructing it in a [[Martez sisters' repair shop|hangar]] the sisters had inherited from their [[Martez family|parents]]. Over [[time]], Trace used the parts she had gathered to build a heavily modified ''Nebula''-class freighter. The ship became Trace's pride and joy, and she gave it the name ''Silver Angel''. In particular, Trace took time to greatly increase the speed of the ''Silver Angel'' via modifications, expecting for some missions to require a speedy getaway. [[File:TraceShip.png|thumb|left|300px|Trace Martez was working on the ''Angel'' when a stranger crashed onto her landing pad.]] Trace was working on her ship in [[19 BBY]] when the [[Force-Sensitive Outcast]] [[Ahsoka Tano]] crashed her [[Ahsoka Tano's speeder bike|Joben T-85 speeder bike]] onto the [[hangar]]'s landing pad. Trace assisted the stranger and introduced herself to the [[Togruta]], who took note of the freighter in the garage and identified it as a ''Nebula''-class. The hopeful pilot was impressed with Tano's [[eye]] for ships and offered to repair her [[Joben T-85 speeder bike|bike]] for a price. The two became quick friends, with Tano saving the young mechanic from the debt collector [[Pintu Son-El]] and assisting her in catching a renegade [[Type II loadlifter droid|binary loadlifter]]—one of three [[droid]]s that Rafa intended to sell to the criminal [[Lokann]]. Although Trace was welcoming to Tano, Rafa did not trust her sister's new companion. ===In service to the Pykes=== {{Quote|Trace, please, I need your help with this.''"
"''You mean, you need the ''best'' pilot around and the ''fastest'' ship you know?''"
"''Yes, to both of those.|Rafa convinces her sister to fly to Kessel|audio=YesToBoth-DND.flac|}} After selling the [[Loader droid|loadlifters]], Rafa made a deal with the [[Pyke Syndicate]] [[crime lord]] [[Marg Krim]] to transport [[sansanna spice]] from the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] planet''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]'' [[Kessel]] to the [[Pyke Palace]] on [[Oba Diah]], a nearby planet that acted as the Syndicate's base of operations. After the [[Unidentified pilot (Rafa Martez)|pilot]] she originally hired pulled out of the job, she was forced to turn to her fledgling-pilot sister, who was not informed of the journey's purpose. Trace was eager to finally pilot her ship and welcomed Tano and Rafa aboard the maiden voyage of the ''Silver Angel'', ignoring her companions' distaste regarding the vessel's name. Despite never having earned a pilot's license, Trace Martez flew her vessel out of Level 1313 and took to the skies. Against Tano's warnings, she piloted the ship into a restricted [[Republic Military|military]] air lane being used by [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry|Low Altitude Assault Transports]] that were boarding a [[Anakin's flagship|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]]. [[Republic Navy]] [[Admiral]] [[Wullf Yularen]], the [[Commanding officer|commander]] of the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|Star Destroyer]], hailed the ''Angel''{{'s}} crew and threatened them with [[Prisoner|incarceration]]. However, they were allowed to pass by [[Jedi General]] [[Anakin Skywalker]], who was aboard the [[Star Destroyer]] and [[Telepathy|sensed]] the presence of Tano, his former [[Padawan|apprentice]], aboard the ''Silver Angel''. [[File:SilverAngelKessel-DND.png|thumb|right|300px|The ''Silver Angel'' lands at the spice mines of Kessel.]] Trace Martez piloted her freighter away from Coruscant and, forgetting to disengage the [[air brake]]s, made the jump to [[hyperspace]], excitedly proclaiming that it was her first time doing so. The brakes made for a rough ride through hyperspace, causing the ship to rumble and creak as it traveled to the Outer Rim. The pilot finally remembered to disengage the brakes after noticing Tano and her sister's discomfort within the ship. The ''Silver Angel'' was brought out of hyperspace and entered the [[Akkadese Maelstrom]], a giant cluster of [[gas]] and debris that surrounded Kessel. Trace landed the vessel at the [[Kessel Castle|palace]] of [[King]] [[Yaruba]], the ruler of the planet. Yaruba's [[majordomo]], [[Kinash Lock]], sent the ''Silver Angel'' and its crew to retrieve shipments of spice from the [[Spice mines of Kessel|mining sector]] of the planet, assuring the cautious Tano that the shipment would be used for medicinal purposes. As Trace made the [[Kessel Run]] to deliver their shipment to Oba Diah, Tano realized that they were delivering to the [[Pyke]]s and told the sisters that the [[gangster]]s were not to be trusted, warning Trace that they might steal her ship. As Tano and Rafa argued over the best course of action, Trace, angered at the possibility of losing the ship she had worked so hard to assemble, dumped the shipment of spice into hyperspace as a result. Rafa, in the wake of losing 30,000 credits worth of spice, threatened Trace with the prospect of giving the ''Angel'' to the Pykes to make up for the lost cargo. At Tano's insistence, however, the crew agreed to continue to Oba Diah and attempt to deceive the Pykes. ===Impounded on Oba Diah=== {{Quote|I never figured when I took my ship out for the first time, I'd wind up in a place like this.|Trace, imprisoned on Oba Diah|audio=PlaceLikeThis-DND.flac|{{TCW|Dangerous Debt}}}} [[File:SilverAngelObaDiah-DND.png|thumb|left|300px|The ''Silver Angel'' arrives at Marg Krim's palace.]] Once the ''Silver Angel'' arrived at the Pyke Palace, Krim greeted the [[spicerunner]]s and demanded to see their cargo. Unbeknownst to the sisters, Tano had used [[the Force]] to perform a [[mind trick]] on Krim, persuading him to pay the sisters without needing to see the shipment. Convinced they were in the clear, Trace told Tano to fire up the ship's engines as she and Rafa unloaded the empty containers. As they began to leave, however, Krim's majordomo, [[Fife]], found his superior's behavior suspicious and demanded that the Pykes be given the codes to open the crates, but Trace began to take off. Fife forced the containers open, and, discovering them to be empty, ordered [[Sarisa-class gunship|''Sarisa''-class gunships]] to block the freighter's escape. Before the ''Silver Angel'' could flee the planet, the Pyke ships caught the vessel within a [[tractor beam]] and captured its crew. Tano and the Martez sisters were thrown into the Pykes' [[Prison|dungeons]] and [[torture]]d to reveal what had happened to their spice. Their ship, meanwhile, was kept on a landing pad outside the palace. The trio managed to [[Escape from Oba Diah|escape]] from their confinement and made their way to the [[Oba Diah city|city]] beneath the Pyke headquarters. As they wandered the seedy streets, Trace Martez climbed on top of a structure and pointed out the ''Angel''{{'s}} silhouette to her companions. Although Trace desired to retrieve her ship, Rafa considered it too dangerous and told her that they should escape on the first vessel they could find. Trace reluctantly agreed on the condition that Rafa would pay for a new ship when they returned home; neither sister would get their wish before the group was once again captured by the Pykes. [[File:MartezStolenSpice-TA.png|thumb|right|300px|The Martez sisters loaded the ''Silver Angel''{{'s}} hold with stolen spice.]] In a bid to free her companions, Tano lied to Krim, telling him that the Martez sisters had hidden the spice on another planet. Krim thus allowed the sisters to leave to retrieve the spice while keeping Tano locked away in the Pyke dungeons. Trace and Rafa boarded the ''Angel'' and departed from Oba Diah for [[Orondia Refueling Station]]. The sisters decided to rescue Tano, but, knowing that they could not return to Krim empty-handed, conspired to trick the unwitting [[Toong]] workers on the Pykes' [[Oba Diah loading docks|shipping docks]] at the [[Fuel|refueling]] station into loading spice onto the ''Angel'', hoping to then bring those shipments to Krim himself. As the sisters landed at the station, Rafa Martez hailed the Toongs from the ''Angel'' under the alias of "Transport 1519" and ordered the workers to perform a "special request pickup." ===Escaping to Coruscant=== {{Dialogue|Trace|We might have lost the rear deflectors, but we still have the front.|Tano|Uh, this isn't a good idea.|Rafa|Yeah. I'm gonna agree with Ahsoka on this one.|attr=The ''Silver Angel'' crew as Trace flew headfirst toward a Pyke ship|src=}} After a small skirmish with the Toongs and their [[Trandoshan]] [[Unidentified Trandoshan manager|manager]] at the docks, the Martez sisters flew to the Pyke Palace with the stolen shipment, eager to rescue Tano and leave Oba Diah for good. However, Krim ordered for their immediate [[Death penalty|execution]] after pressure from his superior, the renegade [[Sith Lord]] [[Maul]]. Tano thus set off a series of [[Bomb|explosives]] across the palace, buying time for the trio to escape to the ''Angel''. Pursued by patrol ships, Trace piloted the freighter through the canyons of Oba Diah, giving control of the ship's rear gun to Tano while Rafa monitored its scanners. Tano destroyed two Pyke ships, but a third ship shot out the ''Angel''{{'s}} gun and rear deflector shields, leaving the ship defenseless from behind. Putting her faith in the front shields, Trace Martez turned the ship around and flew headfirst toward the remaining fighter. As the ''Angel'' barreled forward, the smaller ship veered to the right to avoid a head-on collision and crashed into the [[mountain]]side instead. [[File:SilverAngelEscape-TA.png|thumb|left|300px|During their escape, Trace piloted the ''Silver Angel'' while Tano manned the laser turret.]] Confident in their escape, Trace flew the ship into the planet's upper atmosphere, unaware that they were being followed by a [[Gauntlet (Bo-Katan Kryze)|''Kom'rk''-class fighter/transport]]. The ''Silver Angel'' was flown back to Coruscant and landed in the Martez sisters' hangar, completing its first voyage. As Tano and the Martez sisters discussed their adventure outside the ship, they were interrupted by the [[Mandalorian]] [[Bo-Katan Kryze]], who had followed them from Oba Diah. She requested Tano's help in [[Siege of Mandalore|defeating]] Maul, who had forcibly [[Takeover of Mandalore|taken]] over the planet [[Mandalore]].{{TCW|Shades of Reason}} After bidding Trace and Rafa farewell, Tano departed with Kryze, leaving her [[Speeder bike|bike]] with the sisters. ===Smuggling in a new age=== {{Quote|R7, we're ready for a pickup.|Trace, while escaping from the decommissioning facility|}} In that same [[Standard year|year]], the Clone Wars came to an end when the Republic's [[Supreme Chancellor]], [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]], [[Proclamation of the New Order|proclaimed]] himself [[Galactic Emperor]] and declared all Jedi to be enemies of the state.''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' Under the new [[Galactic Empire]], the Martez sisters fled Coruscant and started life anew aboard the ''Angel'', turning it into a mobile homebase{{Databank|the-silver-angel|The ''Silver Angel''}} to serve their work as [[smuggler]]s. Dedicating themselves to resisting the regime, they also welcomed a new crewmember aboard: [[R7-A7]], the former [[astromech droid]] of Ahsoka Tano.{{Databank|r7-a7|R7-A7}} The group was later sent by the former [[Clone Captain]] [[Rex]]{{TBB|Battle Scars}} to [[Mission to a droid decommissioning facility|obtain]] the remains of a decommissioned [[T-series military strategic analysis and tactics droid|T-series tactical droid]] in [[Coronet City]] on the planet [[Corellia]] to help with his [[Clone Underground|resistance effort]] against the Empire. [[File:IndustrialDockyard-Decommissioned.png|thumb|right|300px|The ''Silver Angel'' delivered the Bad Batch to safety on Corellia.]] Although they were initially able to locate the [[Droid brain|processing unit]] of [[Unidentified T-series tactical droid (Corellia)|one such droid]] in a [[Decommissioning facility|dismantling facility]], complications arose when the sisters encountered the [[Clone Force 99|Bad Batch]], a [[squad]] of rogue [[clone commando]]s that was after the same [[Tactical droid|droid]]. Pursued by [[Imperial Police Droid]]s, the two groups were rescued by R7, who brought the organics aboard the ''Silver Angel'' during the firefight. In the process, however, the tactical droid [[brain]] was destroyed. Fortunately for the sisters, the Batch had copied the droid's information onto a [[data rod]]. Believing that the sisters' quest was a noble one, the [[Cloning|clone]] leader [[Hunter]] trusted them with the intelligence. After dropping the [[clone trooper]]s off at [[Marauder (Omicron-class)|their own ship]], Trace and Rafa departed Corellia aboard the ''Angel'' and sent word to Rex, informing him of their successful mission as well as the [[Cid's Parlor|location]] of the rogue clones. ==Owners and operators== {{Quote|Trace's flying is more of a dream than a reality.''"
"''What did you say?''"
"''Oh, I-I said the ship flies like a dream.|The Martez sisters|audio=LikeADream-DND.flac|}} The ''Silver Angel'' was owned and maintained by the mechanic Trace Martez, who assembled the ship in her family's hangar after her [[Trace and Rafa Martez's mother|mother]] and [[Trace and Rafa Martez's father|father]] were [[Death|killed]] in the collateral damage of the [[Jedi Order]]'s [[Senate hostage crisis|pursuit]] of [[Ziro Desilijic Tiure|Ziro]] the [[Hutt]] that took place in [[21 BBY]].{{TCWcanondates|122}} Martez desired to fly across the [[galaxy]] and viewed the ''Angel'' as her escape from the squalor of Coruscant's underworld and the [[Jedi]] who led wars on the upper levels. [[File:SilverAngelCrewDND.png|thumb|left|300px|The crew of the ''Silver Angel'' discussing the Pykes]] Throughout its mission to and subsequent escape from the Pyke Syndicate, the ship was piloted by Trace Martez while her sister Rafa would often handle the vessel's communication systems and talk her way through dangerous situations. When the ''Angel'' was pursued by Pyke ships on Oba Diah, Trace gave control of the weapons systems to Ahsoka Tano, whose [[Jedi training]] allowed her to swiftly take out their pursuers with the ship's [[turret]]. During the [[Imperial Era]], the droid R7-A7 served aboard the ''Angel'' as co-pilot and resident astromech. While embarking on planetary missions, Trace and Rafa trusted R7 to helm the ship in their absence. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|While there were some components from the design of the ''Silver Angel'' utilized for the ''Ghost'', there was no way that we were going to make the new feature starship in ''Rebels'' a reuse or repurpose of something else. We mainly took control panels and arrangements and reused and repurposed them the same way a live-action set would.|Dave Filoni on the ship's similarities to the ''Ghost''|{{SWYouTube|series=Clone Wars Download|text="Dangerous Debt"|video=06nGLL8rjTE|sw_url=video/clone-wars-download-dangerous-debt}}}} The ''Silver Angel'' was first shown in a television spot for the [[The Clone Wars: Season Seven|seventh season]] of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' animated series on [[March 17]], [[2020]],{{SWYouTube|l77BI2VhmzA|Star Wars: The Clone Wars | Official TV Spot | Disney+}} and later made its debut in "[[Gone with a Trace]]," the fifth episode of the season, released on [[Disney+]] on [[March 20]] of the same year.{{Disney|subdomain=dmedmedia|url=disney-plus/star-wars-the-clone-wars/705|text=Episode 705 "Gone With a Trace"}} The ship was not identified until the next episode, "[[Deal No Deal]]," which was released a week later on [[March 27]].{{WebCite|url=https://comicbook.com/tv-shows/2020/02/20/disney-plus-march-new-arrivals-movies-tv-shows-streaming|text=Everything Coming to Disney+ in March|author=Ridgely, Charlie|date=2020-02-20|work=[https://comicbook.com Comic Book]|archivedate=20200316124412}} On the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars - The Final Season (Episodes 5-8) (Original Soundtrack)|second volume]] of the season's [[Musical score|soundtrack]], the name of the ship is written incorrectly on the fifth track, "Launching the Silverangel."[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars - The Final Season (Episodes 5-8) (Original Soundtrack)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars - The Final Season'' (Episodes 5-8)]] [[File:SACockpitConcept.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Concept art of the ship's cockpit that was later repurposed for ''Star Wars Rebels'']] The ship's cockpit, which was originally designed for a sixth season of the original run of ''The Clone Wars'', was repurposed as the cockpit of the ''[[Ghost]]'', the ship flown by the [[Spectres|main characters]] of [[Lucasfilm Animation]]'s next series, ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'', as they felt its interior worked very well and did not think it would otherwise get to be seen at the time. Nevertheless, the full design of the ''Ghost''{{'s}} cockpit was not an exact replica of ''The Clone Wars'' design. Series creator and executive producer [[Dave Filoni]] clarified that only pieces of the concept were used, much like how a live-action set would repurpose props and layouts. Concept art for the cockpit done by [[Kilian Plunkett]] on [[April 25]], [[2018]] shows that the ''Silver Angel'' was originally named ''Black Ace''. Concept art of the ship's exterior was drawn by [[JP Balmet]],{{SW|url=deal-no-deal-concept-art-gallery|text="Deal No Deal" Concept Art Gallery}} {{C|Slides 1, 8, 10, and 12}} and lighting concepts of the planets featured in the story arc done by [[Jason Boesch]] also include the vessel.{{SW|url=together-again-concept-art-gallery|text="Together Again" Concept Art Gallery}} {{C|Slide 10}} Artist [[Marissa Bernstel]] created storyboards for scenes featuring the ''Silver Angel'' while under contract at [[Lucasfilm Animation]], which were then later sent to animators for the animation process.{{WebCite|url=http://www.mbernstel.com/?cat=4|text=Storyboards|author=[[Marissa Bernstel]]|date=2020-03-04|archivedate=20241205035942}} ===Concept art gallery=== {{Gallery |source=''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' |storyboards= File:SilverAngel-Bernstel1.jpg|Pre-vis reel of the ''Silver Angel'', Marissa Bernstel File:SilverAngel-Bernstel2.jpg|Pre-vis reel of the ''Silver Angel'', Marissa Bernstel |concept= File:SilverAngelConcept.jpg|''Silver Angel'', JP Balmet File:SACockpitConcept.jpg|''Silver Angel'' cockpit, Kilian Plunkett File:JPLightingConcept.jpg|Kessel lighting concept featuring ''Silver Angel'', Jason Boesch File:JPLightingConcept2.jpg|Oba Diah lighting concept featuring ''Silver Angel'', Jason Boesch File:SilverAngelLightingConcept.jpg|''Silver Angel'' lighting concept, Jason Boesch |digital= |in-progress= }} ==Appearances== *{{TCW|Gone with a Trace}} {{1st}} *{{TCW|Deal No Deal}} {{1stID|''Silver Angel''}} *{{TCW|Dangerous Debt}} *{{TCW|Together Again}} *''[[The Clone Wars: Season 7: Volume 1]]'' *{{TBB|Decommissioned}} ==Sources== {{ScrollBox|content= {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Silver Angel}} {{CardGameSet|set={{SWCT|set=Star Wars: The Clone Wars -
